summary: First-pass full backend + frontend test for IronClaw-Security. 17/18 backend pytest cases passed initially; one /api/events/simulate failure was MongoDB ObjectId serialization (fixed by excluding _id from response — see updated_files). After fix: 18/18 pass. Frontend landing, signin, dashboard widgets, purchase API fire, signout, and unauth /dashboard redirect all work. One critical frontend bug: AuthModal does not sync its internal `mode` state when `initialMode` prop changes, so clicking nav-signup-btn / hero-signup-btn opens the modal in SIGNIN mode (not SIGNUP). The signup UI path is therefore effectively broken — users can only sign up via the modal's 'Create an account' link.

minor.issue: Returned 500 because insert_one() mutated event dict with ObjectId _id (then serialization failed). FIXED in /app/backend/server.py by event.pop('_id', None) after insert.

ui_bugs.issue: `mode` is initialized from `initialMode` only on first mount via useState(initialMode). Subsequent prop changes (Landing toggling authMode between 'signin' and 'signup') are ignored, so nav-signup-btn and hero-signup-btn open the modal in SIGNIN mode. Verified visually: modal title shows 'Operator sign in' even after clicking Sign Up. Fix: add `useEffect(() => setMode(initialMode), [initialMode, open])` in /app/frontend/src/components/AuthModal.jsx.

action_items: Fix AuthModal mode sync: add useEffect to update mode whenever initialMode prop or open toggles (critical — signup UI is broken).
Consider showing inline form-error from toast.error so users get feedback when signin fails (currently only sonner toast). Optional.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthModal: useState(initialMode) without an effect to sync prop changes — classic React pitfall. The component is always mounted on Landing (only renders null when !open), so the initializer fires once with initial 'signin'.

server.py create_live_event: insert_one mutates the dict in place and pollutes downstream responses with ObjectId; pattern is repeated elsewhere — recommend always projecting {_id: 0} on reads and stripping _id after writes.
AuthContext probably stores token in localStorage 'ironclaw_token' — verify SSR/cleanup on signout (signout flow works correctly in testing).
Dashboard polling every 20s for /api/events/simulate is intentional but could cause noisy logs / wallet drift; consider gating behind a visibility check (document.visibilityState === 'visible').

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (signup-button-mode bug; signin + dashboard + purchase + signout all work)

rca_of_the_issue: AuthModal RCA: `const [mode, setMode] = useState(initialMode);` only reads initialMode once. Landing.jsx mounts <AuthModal initialMode={authMode} ... /> from initial state, so mode='signin'. When user clicks Sign Up, Landing calls setAuthMode('signup'); setAuthOpen(true). AuthModal re-renders with new initialMode prop but its local `mode` state stays 'signin'. Reproduction: Landing → click Sign Up → modal opens but title 'Operator sign in' and submit calls /api/auth/signin. Mitigation: `useEffect(() => { setMode(initialMode); }, [initialMode, open]);` inside AuthModal. ObjectId RCA: motor's insert_one mutates the inserted document, adding `_id: ObjectId`. The same dict is then returned from the FastAPI endpoint, where jsonable_encoder fails on ObjectId. Mitigation applied: `event.pop('_id', None)` after insert (alternatively, copy dict before insert or project on subsequent reads).
